subject.title: Gateway should not fail to start when optional ElevenLabs/TTS API key is missing

question: Should absent built-in TTS provider API-key SecretRefs degrade only TTS at Gateway startup while auth, model/provider policy, invalid refs, and resolved-shape failures remain fail-closed?
rationale: Current behavior and the linked PR both touch the startup credential fail-closed boundary, which is a product/security decision automation should not finalize alone.

options.title: Approve Scoped TTS Degradation
options.body: Land the linked PR after owner review if missing built-in TTS keys should warn and localize failure to TTS while strict credential failures remain fatal.

options.title: Require Visibility First
options.body: Ask for status, doctor, or audit reporting in the same PR if configured-unavailable visibility is required before changing startup behavior.

options.title: Keep Strict Startup Failure
options.body: Close or reject the linked PR if every active configured SecretRef should remain startup-fatal, including optional TTS provider keys.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped TTS Degradation
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after owner review if missing built-in TTS keys should warn and localize failure to TTS while strict credential failures remain fatal.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the SecretRef runtime assignment semantics introduced in the broad SecretRef coverage work.
